test-01-spec-example.txt.scenario: Example from the assignment sheet (origin 2, goals 5 and 4)

test-02-origin-is-goal.txt.scenario: Origin is also a destination: path is just the origin, cost 0

test-03-no-path.txt.scenario: Goal lies in a separate component, no solution exists

test-04-one-way-trap.txt.scenario: Straight-line route through node 2 is blocked by a one-way edge

test-05-single-edge.txt.scenario: Smallest possible problem: one edge from origin to goal

test-06-equal-cost-goals.txt.scenario: Two goals at the same cost from origin: tie-breaking decides

test-07-cycles.txt.scenario: Bidirectional edges and a triangle: loops must be prevented

test-08-dead-ends.txt.scenario: Several branches end in dead ends before the real route

test-09-long-chain.txt.scenario: A straight chain of 10 nodes, only one route

test-10-diamond-equal-paths.txt.scenario: Two different routes with identical cost: tie-breaking decides the path

test-11-greedy-trap.txt.scenario: Closest-looking node leads to an expensive route: GBFS is not optimal here

test-12-tight-heuristic.txt.scenario: Edge costs equal straight-line distance (Pythagorean triples)

test-14-dense-complete.txt.scenario: Complete directed graph on 7 nodes: many branches per node

test-15-fewer-hops-costs-more.txt.scenario: Direct edge has fewest moves but is far more expensive than the long route

test-16-origin-no-outgoing.txt.scenario: Origin only has incoming edges, so no goal is reachable

test-17-grid-4x4.txt.scenario: 4x4 grid with unit costs: huge number of equal-cost ties

test-18-random-20-nodes.txt.scenario: Seeded random graph, 20 nodes, mixed one-way and two-way edges

test-19-messy-format.txt.scenario: Parser stress test: Windows line endings, blank lines, trailing spaces, non-consecutive ids

test-20-grid-10x10.txt.scenario: 10x10 grid with about 20% of the links removed as walls: large search space, many ties, two goals
